Dear Members of the Bengali Association of North Florida (BANF),

Warm greetings to all.

The Board of Trustees (BOT) writes to you today with a sense of responsibility, transparency, and forward vision regarding the governance of our beloved community organization.

The current bylaws of BANF were last updated in September 2011. In the 14+ years since that revision, our Association has experienced significant growth and transformation — in:
   
   -    
Growing number of Members

   -    
Financial responsibilities

   -    
Scope and scale of cultural events and programs

   -    
Community engagement and outreach initiatives


While this growth is a matter of pride for all of us, it has also highlighted that the existing bylaws no longer fully reflect our present operational realities.

Through our collective experience — including lessons learned from past operational challenges and mistakes — it has become clear that BANF now requires:
   
   -    
Stricter structural guidelines

   -    
Clearer accountability mechanisms

   -    
Well-defined governance processes

   -    
Stronger financial oversight

   -    
Transparent decision-making frameworks


These updates are not about change for the sake of change. They are about ensuring stability, preventing future issues, protecting the Association’s integrity, and building a governance structure that supports the next generation of BANF members.




Why Your Vote Matters

As per the current bylaws, any amendment requires approval from two-thirds (2/3) of all registered members.

This is not merely two-thirds of votes cast — it is two-thirds of the total registered membership. Therefore, every single member’s vote is crucial for the amendment to pass.



Your participation directly determines the future governance of BANF.




You can cast your vote here ----   Please Vote here
***Please note: Voting eligibility is limited to members whose memberships were valid and in good standing through January 31, 2026.***




Timeline & Member Engagement

We strongly encourage all members to review the proposed amendments carefully.
   
   -    
Members will have until March 15 to seek clarifications and cast their vote.

   -    
A detailed Q&A session will be conducted during the upcoming General Body Meeting (GBM).

   -    
Members may also directly contact any Board of Trustee member for clarification prior to voting.


We welcome questions. We welcome discussion. We welcome engagement.



This process is about collective responsibility and shared ownership of BANF’s future.

Below is a concise summary of the most significant upgrades:

Major Structural & Governance Enhancements


   
   -    
Clear Separation of Roles

   -    
Term Limits & Cooling-Off Periods
      
      -       
President: Maximum two consecutive terms with mandatory cooling-off.

      -       
BOT: Structured 6-year terms with staggered continuity.

      -       
EC members: Term caps and cooling-off requirements to prevent concentration of control.


   -    
Revised Election Framework
      
      -       
BOT now oversees elections (replacing the ad-hoc election committee).

      -       
Electronic voting formally permitted.

      -       
Defined quorum rules and run-off election procedures.



  

Financial Oversight & Risk Controls (Significant Upgrade)
   
   -    
Stronger Expense Controls
      
      -       
$2,000+ requires dual authorization.

      -       
$6,000+ requires General Body approval.

      -       
Higher-tier threshold for very large expenditures (proposed additional 2/3 requirement).

      -       
Clear documentation and retention requirements.


   -    
Creation of a Contingency Fund
      
      -       
Separate safeguarded account.

      -       
Capped surplus transfers (up to 25%).

      -       
General Body approval required for any usage.

      -       
Cannot be pledged or used for routine expenses.


   -    
Independent Audit Framework

   
   -    
Independent financial review at least once every six activity cycles.

   -    
Mandatory reporting to the General Body.

   -    
Special audit authority if irregularities are suspected.



Accountability & Compliance Provisions
   
   -    
Formal Conflict of Interest Policy
      
      -       
Mandatory disclosure and recusal requirements.

      -       
Prohibition on financial benefit to EC/BOT members or family.

      -       
Annual written acknowledgment requirement.


   -    
Code of Conduct (New Addition)
      
      -       
Anti-harassment and non-discrimination provisions.

      -       
Enforcement and disciplinary mechanisms.


   -    
Defined Removal & Due Process
      
      -       
Written notice and opportunity to respond required.

      -       
Clear voting thresholds for removal actions.



Legal & Compliance Strengthening
   
   -    
Expanded IRS 501(c)(3) compliance language.

   -    
Non-discrimination protections.

   -    
Indemnification & liability limitation clauses.

   -    
Defined dissolution distribution rules.

   -    
Formal data privacy provisions.



Regards,Swarnendu, Saugata & Sayani
Board of Trustees
Bengal Association of North Florida
